policies.title: No fakematches
policies.text: A function counts only when source compiles to the original bytes with the original compiler. Inline asm, register pins and byte arrays never count. Machine-lifted functions count as matched but stay labelled unreviewed until a person or agent has given them real names and types.

policies.title: Adversarial review of hand-written work
policies.text: A separate reviewer that never saw the author's reasoning judges names, types and readability (ACCEPT / CHANGES / REJECT). Only ACCEPT merges.

policies.title: Whole-ELF verification
policies.text: Every merge rebuilds the ELF and compares it byte for byte with SLPM_666.75. Progress is counted in bytes of code; the function count is shown beside it because small functions inflate it.

phases.title: Foundations
phases.summary: A build that reproduces the original ELF, a scorer that cannot be fooled, the full function table, and names recovered from the 2014 PS3 debug build.

milestones.title: Build without Docker
milestones.desc: ee-gcc 3.2-040921 runs natively; make ends in a byte compare of the whole ELF.

milestones.title: Progress counted in bytes
milestones.desc: tools/progress_bytes.py; the function count alone overstated progress more than three times.

milestones.title: Names from the E3 2014 PS3 debug build
milestones.desc: 25,356 functions and 5,859 types with layouts read from DWARF; about 7,600 mapped to PS2 functions with a graded confidence.

milestones.title: Full function table
milestones.desc: layout.tsv regenerated from seven evidence sources, 11,286 to 14,618 rows.

milestones.title: Matching rig
milestones.desc: compile_diff (80 ms scorer), get_context, promote with rollback, park, permuter, held-out bench.

milestones.title: Machine lifter
milestones.desc: A deterministic assembly-to-C lifter plus twin transfer and an offline permuter; about 1,480 functions landed without a language model.

phases.title: Putting the house in order
phases.summary: The project moves to the working method of the Four Swords Adventures decompilation: one rule book, a gate, adversarial review, whole-file ownership and structural progress before byte matching.

milestones.title: Standalone repository, rules and site
milestones.desc: One matching branch, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, rules card, review brief, this website.

milestones.title: Non-matching lane
milestones.desc: Functions that compile but do not yet match are kept in nonmatching/, scored by tools/lane.py, never linked. 4,305 lifter candidates came in with it.

milestones.title: Structural progress metric
milestones.desc: Partial credit for functions whose only differences are register choice or instruction order, shown beside the matched figure. First version in tools/lane.py; delay-slot and stack-frame classes to come.

milestones.title: Mechanical gate
milestones.desc: tools/gate.py rebuilds and compares the ELF, refuses a drop in progress, asm, register pins, byte arrays, renamed real names, and (for worker branches) edits to shared files.

milestones.title: Real source files
milestones.desc: The E3 debug build gives 588 original source files. Functions move out of src/anon and src/autodecomp into the file that owned them.

milestones.title: Grinder
milestones.desc: Lean worker sessions with write, structure and match lanes, a judge that keeps any improvement, and a reviewer per kept change.

phases.title: Small functions
phases.summary: Everything under 200 bytes, mostly accessors, thin wrappers and constructors.

milestones.title: Under 80 bytes
milestones.desc: Stubs, getters and setters.

milestones.title: 80 to 199 bytes
milestones.desc: Twin-adjacent functions; the lifter and small-model workers do most of these.

phases.title: Understanding the compiler
phases.summary: Nearly every unsolved difference is register colouring or delay-slot fill. The answer is to read the compiler, write down the model and search with it, before any more agent waves.

milestones.title: Register allocator model
milestones.desc: Verify the GCC 3.2 global.c priority formula against the Sony build with RTL dumps; write docs/REGALLOC.md.

milestones.title: Mechanical search at scale
milestones.desc: Permuter and flag sweep over every near-miss; search finds the form, a model names and tidies it.

phases.title: The bulk of the game
phases.summary: Functions of 200 bytes and more hold almost two thirds of the code. Whole-file work, structure first.

milestones.title: 200 to 999 bytes
milestones.desc: Whole-file workers; structurally right first, byte match second.

milestones.title: 1 KB and more
milestones.desc: Large functions cut into pieces by source statement and solved piecemeal.

milestones.title: VU0 and MMI functions
milestones.desc: About 680 functions use vector-unit or multimedia instructions the C compiler never emits from plain C.

phases.title: The whole game
phases.summary: Data owned by its files, a real link, the overlays, and a behaviour check against the original.

milestones.title: Files own their data
milestones.desc: Rodata, data and bss rebuilt from source instead of copied from the original.

milestones.title: The five overlays
milestones.desc: gumibattle, gumimenu, shop, title and movie; about 1.05 MB and 4,700 functions in OVL.IMG.

milestones.title: Behaviour harness
milestones.desc: The original and our build run side by side in PCSX2 on the same inputs.

milestones.title: SLPM_666.75 from source
milestones.desc: Every function matched.
